findings.title: getVoiceDemandSnapshot.observedAt is a frozen data timestamp, never an observation clock, so the 90s stale gate permanently wins
findings.detail: NOT FIXED — byte-identical to the round-1 head. observedAt = String(currentRows.at(-1)?.updated_at ?? '') || events.at(-1)?.observedAt || source.created_at; with no voice_sessions rows it is voice_health_demand_source.created_at, set once with new Date().toISOString() at migration (StateStore.ts:7917-7924), i.e. deploy time, forever. PROVEN against the real helper: four consecutive record-demand refreshes (state=none, refreshObservedAt=true) with the frozen observedAt the Bridge would send produced four change rows (changeSeq 2,3,4,5) EVERY ONE stamped changedAt=2026-09-20T08:00:00.000Z, demand_observed_at stayed frozen, and the resulting projectView max over [demandObservedAt, lastIterationSuccessAt=null, lastProgressAt=null, lastFailureAt=null, bootAt, last changedAt] was 2026-09-20T08:00:01.000Z and never advances. So 90s after deploy the Epic page permanently renders '语音读数过期；无法确认当前语音健康', the '无会话需求，正常休眠' branch plan section 3 requires for the FLY-2701 on-demand model is unreachable, and any open incident is replaced by that text (see render-stale-branch-drops-active-incidents). Every epic-page test hand-supplies observedAt: EPIC_SHAPE_NOW, so the real derivation has no coverage.

findings.title: The unknown/stale/unavailable early-return precedes the unhealthy branch, so HTML and Markdown silently drop every active incident the JSON still carries
findings.detail: NOT FIXED — byte-identical (render-html.ts:617-626, render-markdown.ts:577-583). renderVoiceHealth returns a bare '无法确认当前语音健康' paragraph when sourceStatus==='unavailable' || status==='unknown' || demandState==='unknown' || stale, before the status==='unhealthy' incident block at render-html.ts:630 / render-markdown.ts:585. Reachable without any staleness: on ANY projector exception (a single 500ms python3 execFile timeout suffices) markVoiceHealthProjectionUnavailable flips the cursor, and getVoiceHealthProjection (StateStore.ts:16697-16714) deliberately RETAINS the fault — sourceStatus 'unavailable', status 'unhealthy', activeIncidents: prior.activeIncidents. The renderer discards those retained incidents in both human-facing surfaces while page.voiceHealth.value in the JSON still lists them with their delivery state. The sibling renderDeployment (render-html.ts:548-580) does the opposite: it keeps rendering active rows and puts the caveat in the note line. Plan section 5 requires 长时间故障由固定页持续展示 and 优先保留活动故障/投递未知.

findings.title: trigger_invalid / change_gap / demand_overflow snapshots are discarded in the Bridge, so a dropped trigger renders as dormant instead of unknown
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. The author's own follow-ups.md:27 records this verbatim as deferred ('demand-source-degradation-never-reaches-health-source ... 不能把它宣称为全部 demand-source degradation 覆盖'), classified MEDIUM; I keep HIGH because it defeats the R1 blocking acceptance criterion in their own plan. voiceHealthDemandPayload throws voice_demand_source_unavailable for sourceStatus !== 'available' and VoiceSessionRuntime.projectVoiceDemand (voice-session-runtime.ts:180-188) catches every recorder error, logs '[voice-session] demand projection failed' and returns without advancing the cursor, so the three fail-closed states never reach the helper; it keeps its previous demand_state with source_status='available' and projectView (voice-health-projector.ts:351-358) emits 'dormant'. Failure: drop voice_health_demand_sessions_update while demand_state is 'none', then create voice sessions — every poll_failed/session_failed episode is demand-gated (voice-health.py:2498, 2577, 1799) and never opens while the page reports '无会话需求，正常休眠'. Amplifier confirmed by probe: record-demand is the only writer that creates the health row, so on a host whose demand source is fail-closed from the start the row is never created and every projector tick dies before the 60s startup guard (see null-current-projection-rejected-as-record). voice-health-projector.test.ts:98 and :644 cover the digest-mismatch and unknown-demand cases, which travel a different path.

findings.title: A claimed/warming session with a renewing lease is excluded from the 60s startup_not_ready guard forever and is rendered healthy
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. CONFIRMED FIRST-HAND at this head: the shipped test 'does not report an old claimed/warming session while its daemon lease is active' (voice-health-projector.test.ts:221) passes for both states — a 120-second-old warming session with a live lease invokes only 'evaluate' and produces NO startup_not_ready record. The waiting filter skips any claimed/warming session whose leaseExpiresAt is in the future, and SessionLifetime.renew() refreshes the lease every leaseRenewMs, so the exclusion is permanent — contradicting plan section 3 ('claimed/warming不能充当live；超过60秒仍未live产生startup_not_ready' and '不能靠进程/claim刷新此界限'). Compounding it, daemon.ts:247-255 emits a progress observation for claimed|warming|live, voice-health.py:2587 sets phase='active', and voice-health-projector.ts:362 maps phase==='active' to status 'healthy'. Failure: session.start() hangs (discord guild fetch, or RealtimeFrontend.start()/Codex app-server request — neither bounded), renew keeps returning 'warming', and sweepVoiceSessions (StateStore.ts:4427) only fails sessions on lease expiry. The founder sits alone in the voice channel while the page says '有会话需求，语音健康正常' and no alert is ever sent; evaluate_health cannot catch it either because its active branch anchors on last_progress_at, refreshed every 4s. Needs a decision (e.g. cap the exclusion at createdAt + 60s + presenceGraceMs), not a silent patch.

findings.title: A lease-renew progress zeroes failure_streak AND re-anchors first_failure_at, defeating both alert thresholds
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. REPRODUCED against the real helper with demand_state=required: poll_failed 09:00:10 (streak 1), poll_failed 09:00:20 (streak 2), one progress 09:00:25 -> streak 0 and first_failure_at cleared, poll_failed 09:00:30 (streak 1), poll_failed 09:00:40 (streak 2). Final state: failureCount=4, failureStreak=2, firstFailureAt re-anchored to 09:00:30, openEpisodes=[] — four consecutive failures in 30 seconds, ZERO incidents, ZERO alerts. evaluate at 09:01:20 (+70s past the real first failure) also returned no_action because the 60s guard reads the re-anchored first_failure_at. Both thresholds in record_result (failure_streak >= 3 at :2498, observedAt - first_failure_at >= 60 at :2503) and evaluate_health's failed_retrying branch (:1892-1896, which additionally bails when last_progress_at > first_failure_at) are defeated by one unrelated lease renew. Plan section 3: '每次成功lease renew只更新内存lastProgressAt ... 不清除未被完整成功验证的故障'. voice-health.test.py:2673 asserts the wrong behaviour.

findings.title: One unexpected file in the pending spool directory permanently disables the entire daemon-side health reporter across every restart
findings.detail: NEW this round. censusSafeFiles throws on ANY directory entry not matching ^[a-f0-9]{64}\.json$ (:1092). writeAtomic creates its scratch file as `.${randomUUID()}.tmp` in that same directory (:995) and removes it only in a finally block, so a SIGKILL between open and rm leaves a permanent non-matching entry; a .DS_Store on the founder's Mac does the same. loadPendingSpools catches, calls signalUnavailable and returns false, which sets filesystemBlocked (:338-340) — and that runs exactly once per process behind the replayLoaded guard. The consequences compound: registerBoot returns false at :342-345 BEFORE startWatchdog(), so there is no 60s evaluate watchdog and no maintenance checkpoint for the process lifetime; queueAvailable() short-circuits at :776 so no observation is ever queued; and cli.ts:139 does `await health.registerBoot();` discarding the boolean. The only evidence is one console.error line (cli.ts:117-121). Net: after an ordinary crash the daemon runs for days emitting zero health data and never self-heals on restart, until an operator manually deletes the stray file. Not a false-green (the page degrades to stale/unknown), but it silently removes the daemon-side half of the feature in exactly the crash-recovery situation the feature exists for. Restrict the census to the expected filename set (ignore, or clean up, unmatched entries) instead of failing the whole load.

findings.title: record_startup opens an episode only if demand_state is 'required' at that instant, and the duplicate short-circuit prevents re-evaluation
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. record_startup bumps phase='startup_failed', failure_count and operation='startup' even when demand is not 'required', but opens no episode and mints no intent, while still inserting the startup_events row — so every later call with the same stable startupAttemptId (= session.sessionId, voice-health-projector.ts:823) returns duplicate (:1732-1757) and re-evaluates nothing. Trigger: record-demand failing across the 60s window (execFile timeout is 500ms for a python3 cold start) leaves demand_state at 'none'. Result: no Discord alert and no incident for a session that never goes live, and since a 'desired' row is never swept by sweepVoiceSessions there is no later failed transition to re-open it. The page then shows dormant, because projectView puts demandState==='none' ahead of the phase checks, hiding phase:'startup_failed'.

findings.title: no_action() inserts the producer_events row, so a recovery observation is consumed permanently and its incident can never be cleared
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. REPRODUCED: demand required with identity (m1,s1); session_failed(m1,s1) opens a session_unavailable episode with a pending intent; session_recovered(m1 -> successor s2) arriving while the snapshot still lists s1 returns 'no_action' and burns producerEventSeq 2; after the Bridge publishes s2, retrying the identical event returns 'duplicate' with no effect. Final state: the episode is STILL OPEN and the intent STILL 'pending' — a session that genuinely recovered leaves a permanent incident on the fixed page and an alert that can never be cleared by the legitimate recovery path. health.ts:665-688 accepts 'no_action' and splices the event out of its spool document, so the daemon never retries it either (my retry was manual). The pure race is narrow because the 3s demand tick usually publishes the successor first, but it widens to routine whenever demand_state is stale — which fail-closed-demand-never-reaches-helper makes reachable.

findings.title: A session_ended event writes last_iteration_success_at and success_count, the poll-scope success markers
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. UPDATE health SET phase='session_ended', last_iteration_success_at = ?, last_progress_at = ?, success_count = success_count + 1 ... driven by a session-scope observation. Plan section 3 requires session recovery to write an independent sessionRecoveryProof '而不是伪造lastIterationSuccessAt', and the session_recovered branch (:2762) correctly touches only last_progress_at. Effect: the fixed page can display '最近完整成功: <now>' while the poll dependency has never succeeded and its poll_dependency episode is still open, and the heartbeat_stale anchor in evaluate_health's idle branch (:1898) is reset by an event that proves nothing about the desired poll.

findings.title: evaluate_health has no staleness branch for starting / session_ended / session_failed / dormant / stopped
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. Only failed_retrying, idle and active are evaluated; every other phase falls to 'else: return response' (no_action) at any horizon. Combined with voice-health-projector.ts:362 mapping phase==='session_ended' unconditionally to status 'healthy', a daemon that freezes in one of those phases produces no local staleness evidence whatsoever. The only backstop is the Bridge-side 60s demand guard — which warming-lease-suppresses-startup-guard defeats for claimed/warming. Plan section 3: '首启无记录有60秒宽限，缺字段为unknown，不为健康' — there is no expiry of that grace. (The heartbeat_stale producer itself DOES work for idle and active; I verified it — see follow-ups-claims-heartbeat-stale-has-no-producer.)

findings.title: No retention anywhere in the source store, and the 20s demand refresh appends a no-op change row plus triggers an Epic-page refresh every 60s
findings.detail: NOT FIXED; deferred by the author at follow-ups.md:29 ('voice-health-store-has-no-retention'). The 'refreshed' branch calls _append_change unconditionally with the frozen observedAt — observed directly in my probe: four refreshes produced four byte-identical change rows. That is ~3 rows/min, ~4300/day, each a full projection snapshot of ~1-2KB; voice-health.py contains no DELETE for changes / producer_events / notification_attempts / demand_transition_events / startup_events, with wal_autocheckpoint=0 (:222) and checkpoint=False on the hot path. Measured ~1.6KB per observation => ~6MB/day steady state. Plan section 3 assumes retention exists ('retention不得删未消费事件'; test_export_rejects_deleted_change_ranges anticipates pruning). Downstream, applyVoiceHealthProjection (StateStore.ts:16589-16594) sets changed = ... || cursor.cursor !== input.cursor, true every run, so requestRefresh fires every 60s forever on a byte-identical payload — bounded by the refresher's 5s debounce and coalescing to one regeneration+publish per minute, and currently skipped for Linear-unbound projects, but an indefinite no-op publish loop once bound.

findings.title: A curl transport failure (exit 6/7, provably nothing sent) is collapsed to delivery_unknown, which is never retried and never re-minted
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. voice_post_discord's exit status is discarded into VOICE_HTTP_CODE='000' and routed to record_voice_source_delivery delivery_unknown. delivery_unknown is absent from CLAIMABLE_STATES (voice-health.py:85 = {pending, queued_transient, config_error}) and from retryableIntentIds (voice-health-projector.ts:385-391), and _open_episode (:2098-2104) returns the existing episode's existing intent while the episode stays open, so no new intent is minted. No meta-alert fires, and 'delivery_unknown channel_id=... binding_digest=...' matches SAFE_ALERT_RECEIPT so the Bridge does not even log. Failure: the host's network drops — exactly the condition that opens the episode — curl exits 7 and the alert is lost for the whole episode. Plan section 4 draws the line at '明确未发送/429可以按既有队列重试'; curl exit 6/7 is 明确未发送 and the evidence is discarded. Fix: capture curl's exit status and route 6/7 only to queued_transient.

findings.title: Bootstrap startup-spool events are imported only when there is exactly one demand identity
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. readStartupEvents() is invoked only under demandState==='required' && sourceStatus==='available' && identities.length === 1. With zero or two-or-more concurrent voice demands, wrapper-level startup failures (startup_config_invalid from flywheel-voice-wrapper.sh:24, etc.) are never imported, never alerted and never archived. The writer caps the spool at 128 files / 1MB (voice-health-startup-spool.py:141-145) and the overflow is swallowed by '|| true', so once saturated, later startup failures are dropped with only stderr. Plan section 4's bootstrap path expects unconditional import keyed on the Bridge's own demand association. Separately, spool/consumed/ (created at :652) has no pruning owner.

findings.title: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is constructed with no root while every sibling in the same call gets FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR, so an isolated Bridge reads and can consume the host's production spool
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. plugin.ts:7215 computes voiceHealthStateRoot from FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR?.trim() || ~/.flywheel and passes it to readExport and the guard; three lines later readStartupEvents: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is called with no argument and the reader resolves join(input.homeDir ?? homedir(), '.flywheel', 'voice-startup-spool') (voice-health-projector.ts:522-529), never consulting FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR. scripts/test-deploy.sh:1598 gives a 529 slot Bridge FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR=${state} with no HOME override, so a slot Bridge reads the founder's real spool on every tick, including the blocking startup tick. If that slot's own store reports demandState 'required' / sourceStatus 'available' with exactly one identity (:751-755) it wins the .consumer.lock flock, records the production startup failure into the SLOT's health DB, and renames the production document into consumed/ (:652-660) — after which the production Bridge never mints the intent. Honest boundary: the cross-root read is unconditional and certain; the consume branch is reachable but I could not construct a slot run that reaches it, and evidence is archived rather than deleted. The homeDir parameter already exists and is used by voice-health-startup-spool-reader.test.ts:33. follow-ups.md:16 records a related deferred item warning this lock is not cross-root ownership proof.

findings.title: validateExport's `currentProjection === undefined` guard does not catch the helper's JSON null, so a source with no health row fails every tick
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. Probed against a virgin state root: export returns "currentProjection":null (voice-health.py:3290 -> _current_projection returns None at :842 when the health row is absent). validateExport's check `(!raw.hasMore && raw.currentProjection === undefined)` uses strict equality so null passes, then record(exported.currentProjection, ...) throws in BOTH projectView (:252) and the Bridge guard (:745) — the latter BEFORE the 60s startup_not_ready waiting block. Effect on a source with no health row: the projector throws, marks the projection unavailable, logs every tick, the page shows '无法确认当前语音健康' rather than the intended '尚未采集', and the 60s guard plus the startup-spool import never run. Normally self-heals because record-demand creates the health row (confirmed by probe) and VoiceSessionRuntime.start() fires at plugin.ts:9343 before the awaited startup tick at :13414 — so the practical exposure is the startup race plus any host where record-demand can never succeed.

findings.title: sourceStatus 'truncated' renders byte-identical to 'complete'; dropped episodes get no warning
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. projectView sets truncated when openEpisodesTruncated || notificationsTruncated || openEpisodes.length > MAX_VOICE_HEALTH_ACTIVE_INCIDENTS (:369-375) and slices to 32 at :312, but neither renderVoiceHealth reads sourceStatus except for the 'unavailable' branch. 40 open episodes render as 32 with 8 silently gone. Plan section 5 requires the 截断警示 and renderDeployment emits '状态已截断（展示 N/M）'. Aggravating: VoiceHealthView (model.ts:369-386) has no retained/total counterparts to ShuttleDeploymentView, so a warning cannot state the magnitude without a model change.

findings.title: Every record_result branch writes source_status='available', erasing record_demand's fail-closed demand_source_unavailable marker
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. record_demand's mismatch path deliberately sets source_status='unavailable', reason_class='demand_source_unavailable', but every record_result branch (idle_success :2456, poll_failed :2477, session_failed :2517, progress :2592, session_recovered/session_ended :2773, closed_not_required :2810, daemon_stopped :2816) writes source_status='available', and idle_success additionally writes reason_class=NULL. Verified: a same-revision/different-digest snapshot gives {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: demand_source_unavailable}; one ordinary idle_success later gives {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: available, reasonClass: null}. Only demandState survives (which keeps this out of HIGH), but sourceStatus==='available' is load-bearing in the projector's startup-spool guard at :753.

findings.title: pause() never detaches its abort listener on the timer path, and this PR newly feeds it a long-lived AbortSignal on every idle poll
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred by the author at follow-ups.md:31). pause() registers signal.addEventListener('abort', fn, {once:true}) and returns on the timer path WITHOUT removeEventListener; {once:true} only detaches after the event fires, and abort fires once at shutdown. This PR introduced the exposure: pre-PR daemon.ts called options.sleep(idlePollMs) with NO signal (verified against e82193650:daemon.ts:244,309), whereas the new run() passes this.sleepController.signal — one AbortController per daemon (daemon.ts:302) — at daemon.ts:326 (idle poll) and :348 (failure backoff), and cli.ts:357 wires sleep: pause. One listener is permanently retained per idle poll: 12/min at the FLYWHEEL_VOICE_IDLE_POLL_MS default of 5000, ~17k/day, each closing over a distinct timer handle and resolve. I checked: Node emits NO MaxListenersExceededWarning for AbortSignal at 40 listeners, so the growth is silent; on shutdown all accumulated listeners fire at once. One removeEventListener in the timer path closes it.

findings.title: claim/renew install the lease from an unvalidated body.leaseTtlMs, so a malformed 2xx produces a NaN deadline that never fences plus a 1ms timer spin
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. This PR rewrote the request layer specifically so a 2xx is not assumed successful and added strict decoding for /desired (decodeDesired at :153), but claim (:306), renew (:332) and renewRecovered (:352) still pass body.leaseTtlMs straight into VoiceLease.install, whose only typing is a compile-time generic on a network response. With leaseTtlMs absent or non-numeric, deadlineMs = sentAt + NaN - timeout = NaN (:105); VoiceLease.assert() then evaluates `!active || monoNow() >= NaN` = false and never throws, so the fence — the mechanism stopping two daemons from both believing they hold authority — is silently disabled for the session. SessionLifetime.armDeadline (daemon.ts:214-228) re-arms with lease.remainingMs = NaN, which Node coerces to a 1ms delay, producing a ~1000/s re-arm spin. A Number.isSafeInteger guard in install() closes both.

findings.title: record_delivery has no post-timeout idempotency key, so a worker cannot confirm its own committed write
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. The authorization side is sound — 'sent' requires a matching claim_token, matching binding_digest, intent['channel_id'] == channel_id and snowflake-validated ids, so no fabricated success — but the UPDATE clears claim_token, claimed_at and claim_expires_at. A retry after a 500ms execFile timeout that actually committed returns notification_claim_mismatch, indistinguishable from a genuinely wrong claim. Plan section 3 requires '超时后不能假设未提交：用 ... 重试查询去重记录'. Every other mutating command has such a key (generation+producerEventSeq, startupAttemptId, revision/cursor, claim token).

findings.title: voice_health_demand_events is retention-protected forever while the consuming cursor is in-memory, so Bridge restarts replay the whole history
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/teamlead/voice_health_demand_events.json classifies the table protectedCurrentOrReference, which fly-2006-retention-loader.mjs treats as a non-delete category — so the append-only trigger log in the shared production teamlead DB grows one row per voice_sessions insert/delete/state/reason/cancel/ending/ended change, forever. VoiceSessionRuntime.demandCursor is a plain in-memory field reset to 0 on every Bridge restart, and projectVoiceDemand drains one 200-event page per 3s tick, so catch-up after restart costs N/200 x 3s for N lifetime events. During catch-up refreshObservedAt is false (events non-empty) so demand_observed_at is not refreshed — which, given the 90s gate in stale-gate-uses-frozen-data-clock, means the page shows '读数过期' for the entire catch-up window. Plan section 3 anticipated retention that deletes consumed events only.

findings.title: demandEvent() drops cancelRequested / endingStarted / previousState, so the helper cannot tell a cancelled demand from a dependency failure
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. The trigger records cancel_requested, ending_started, ended and old_state (StateStore.ts:2810-2859) precisely so the helper can distinguish 'user cancelled' from 'system failed it', but the recorder forwards only eventSeq/eventKind/demandId/attemptId/observedAt (+reasonClass for 'failed'). Failure: a founder cancels a meeting, the session goes ending then times out, and voiceHealthReasonClass maps ending_timeout to session_runtime_failed — the helper opens a session_unavailable incident and pages the engineering channel for a user-initiated cancel. Plan section 3 (防止失败后自动消警) requires the cancel fact to be carried into the record.

findings.title: claim/setState/outbound/receipt failures propagate to the poll path and are recorded as poll_dependency, which a later idle_success closes
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. runOnce() lets bridge.claim() and the lifetime bridge calls throw out to run()'s catch, where pollFailure() records kind:'poll_failed' carrying the diagnostic's operation (claim/state/outbound/receipt). voice-health.py:2498 opens a poll_dependency episode for those, and _close_poll_episode closes it on the next idle_success — so a failure to join the room is cleared by an unrelated idle poll, the scope-isolation outcome plan section 3 forbids. Partially mitigated because the demand path independently opens session_unavailable on required->failed and the 60s waiting guard covers 'desired' sessions, so this is noise plus premature recovery rather than total blindness.

findings.title: A failure to report the terminal session state to the Bridge is swallowed with no health observation
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. Both terminal paths wrap bridge.setState in try/catch, set terminalConfirmed=false and only console.error('[voice] session terminal receipt unavailable; recovery state retained'). Before this change the error propagated out of runOnce and was counted by run()'s catch. Now the Bridge round-trip failure produces no poll_failed and no session_failed observation, no episode and no alert — a whole class of bridge_* failures on the terminal path is invisible to the ledger this change exists to build. recover() (daemon.ts:365-413) likewise emits no health observation on the equivalent path.

findings.title: A 135s real-wall-clock test whose iteration-count assertion tolerates only one lost iteration
findings.detail: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. Commit 868800fff (the only code change since my last review) replaced the per-entry host-clock comparison with a set-membership check on submitted observedAt values — I verified that fix is correct and effective: required-wall-clock-thresholds.test.ts passes 1/1 locally at this head, the new assertion is sound (lastIterationSuccessAt always originates from a submitted observation via both the direct branch in observeNormal and the flushAggregate branch), and it does not weaken the heartbeat coverage. But the flakiness substance is untouched: RUN_FOR_MS is still 135_000 (:20) with await sleep(5000) per iteration, and the assertions are still successes >= 26 (:70) and lastHeartbeat.successCount >= 24 (:95). At zero overhead the loop yields exactly 27 iterations, so the margin is ONE lost iteration; ~185ms average per-iteration drift drops it to 26 and ~400ms drops it to 25 and fails — while each iteration drives an fsync'd atomic spool write and a python3 spawn on the drain path. Honest counter-evidence: it has now been green on CI twice (Unit (light) 7m9s of a 25-minute budget) and three times locally at 135.2-135.5s. Deriving the expected count from measured elapsed time would remove the risk entirely.

findings.title: config_error and invalid receipts retry every 30s forever with no cap, no backoff and no dead-letter transition
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred at follow-ups.md:32). VoiceHealthAlertDispatcher.drain treats config_error and any unparsable receipt as a retry and calls scheduleRetry with a fixed 30s delay, unbounded. lead-alert.sh returns config_error for permanent conditions (missing helper, failed route preflight, invalid frozen payload), so a misconfigured route spawns /bin/bash lead-alert.sh every 30s for the daemon's lifetime; the Bridge does the same every 60s (voice-health-projector.ts:385-392). claim_notification increments attempt_count but nothing enforces a limit or a dead_lettered transition. meta-alert.sh's 10-minute per-reason debounce bounds the alert noise, but not the process churn or the growing attempt_count.

findings.title: The voice-health tick is the only projector awaited ahead of gatePoller.start(); bounded, but an unnecessary boot dependency
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. Bounded and not a real availability risk, per measurement. Ceiling is ~265 sequential helper calls (two drains of <=32 pages, 1 evaluate, <=128 spool record-startup, <=8 waiting record-startup), each capped by execFile timeout: 500 (:413, :708) plus <=128 lock acquisitions at readyTimeoutMs: 500 (:626) — ~196s absolute worst case, but that requires all 265 calls to SUCCEED just under 500ms, since any rejection short-circuits run() into markVoiceHealthProjectionUnavailable. No hang risk: scripts/lib/voice-health.py has zero hits for subprocess|Popen|os.system|os.fork. Measured ~45ms/call, so a typical boot is ~0.15s and a full 128-event spool ~6-12s. Flagged only because the two sibling projectors constructed just above (:12199-12201) live solely in the async 3s poller, whose rejections GatePoller already catches and logs (gate-poller.ts:640-647); dropping the pre-start await costs at most one poll cycle of freshness.

findings.title: The new TypeScript route/bindingDigest module has zero production importers
findings.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred at follow-ups.md:30). A repo-wide grep for 'voice-health-alert-route' outside dist finds exactly one importer: packages/teamlead/src/__tests__/voice-health-alert-delivery.test.ts. Production route resolution happens entirely in scripts/lead-alert.sh via node scripts/shuttle-route-bindings.mjs, and the bindingDigest persisted and revalidated by the helper comes from that shell path — not from resolveVoiceHealthAlertRoute, which computes a different digest (sha256 over {schemaVersion, originProject, route}). The repo now carries two independent definitions of the same contract, only one of which ships. Coverage of the shipped path is not missing (scripts/__tests__/voice-health-alert-route.test.sh exercises the real shell sender and passes), so the cost is drift risk plus a TS test that looks like production routing coverage but is not. Wire it up or delete it.

findings.title: main() reads stdin unconditionally for every subcommand, so any caller that does not close stdin hangs forever with no deadline
findings.detail: NEW this round. `payload = _read_payload()` runs before the command dispatch, so even `init` — which then requires the payload to be None or {} — blocks on an open stdin. PROVEN: `timeout 4 python3 scripts/lib/voice-health.py --state-root $TMP init < <(sleep 30)` exits 124 (hung), while the same command with `</dev/null` exits 0. The helper has no internal deadline. Production callers are safe (the TS clients call child.stdin.end() and additionally bound with timeout: 500; lead-alert.sh pipes via printf which closes stdin), but the author documented in engineering/doc/milestones/FLY-2693.md that this already cost them debugging time on macOS, and any future runbook, cron or QA script that invokes the helper without redirecting stdin will hang indefinitely. Read stdin only for the commands that take a payload, or only when it is not a TTY.

findings.title: A shipped follow-ups entry asserts heartbeat_stale has no producer; it does
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. follow-ups.md:28 states '保留 follow-up MEDIUM heartbeat-stale-never-produced：heartbeat_stale reason 已声明但尚无 producer'. I disproved this against the real helper: register-boot, record-demand(required), one idle_success at 10:00:10, then evaluate at 10:00:50 -> no_action (correct, <60s); evaluate at 10:01:30 -> status=recorded, episode.reasonClass=heartbeat_stale, with a notification intent minted; evaluate at 10:05:00 -> no_action (correct, episode already open). evaluate_health's idle and active branches (voice-health.py:1898, :1903) are the producers, and both the Bridge guard (voice-health-projector.ts:739) and the daemon watchdog (health.ts:425) call evaluate. The real gap is narrower and already covered by evaluate-missing-stale-branch-for-terminal-phases. This matters because the document ships with the change and a Lead prioritising follow-ups would schedule work to build a producer that already exists.

findings.title: reportFatalStartupFailure discards the error entirely, leaving zero diagnostic for a daemon that will not start
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. The parameter is named _error and the log line is the constant '[voice] fatal reasonClass=startup_not_ready operation=startup'; the spool record carries only the reasonClass. This follows plan section 3's rule that raw Error.message must not reach stderr, and package-onboard-smoke.test.sh:232 asserts the exact string. The cost is that 'voice will not start' — the originating FLY-2693 symptom — produces no locally recoverable detail anywhere. A bounded closed-vocabulary classifier (e.g. mapping the known config errors to startup_config_invalid) would keep the sanitization and restore triage.

findings.title: validateVoiceBridgeUrl hard-fails any non-loopback BRIDGE_URL with no allowlist
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. loadVoiceDaemonConfig throws voice_bridge_url_invalid for any host that is not localhost, [::1] or 127.x.x.x, which the wrapper turns into voice_config_invalid and exit 0. Plan section 2 said '生产默认loopback' and '跨主机部署如存在，按现有可信配置明确allowlist'; no allowlist was implemented, so this is an unannounced hard break for any host configuring a non-loopback Bridge. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 is also unmatched.

findings.title: The voice alert lane silently inherits SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE as a permission-preflight override
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. VOICE_HEALTH_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-${SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-} means a stale or leaked SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE in the environment also replaces the real Discord VIEW_CHANNEL/SEND_MESSAGES preflight for voice alerts (shuttle-route-bindings.mjs:301-309). A QA harness that exports it and forgets to unset it downgrades a second production lane's sender check with no signal.

findings.title: The frozen-payload openedAt gate is prefix-only while every sibling field is fully anchored
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T") has no end anchor, and the value is interpolated into the Discord BODY at :778. Not exploitable today — the writer validates via _parse_timestamp (voice-health.py:714), jq -n --arg prevents payload injection, and allowed_mentions:{parse:[]} blocks pings — but it is the one unanchored field in an otherwise closed-vocabulary gate. Related latent fragility: jq errors with exit 5 on `null | test(...)`, so any _open_episode call site leaving health.operation NULL would make its alert permanently undeliverable as 'frozen notification payload is invalid'; I re-checked all five call sites and each sets operation first, so this is latent only.

findings.title: The demand digest omits project_name and meeting_id, and neither column is in the trigger's UPDATE OF list
findings.detail: NOT FIXED, and deliberate: follow-ups.md:14 dispositions this as '已处理 demand-digest-field-scope-undefined ... 无关字段更新不改变 revision/digest'. Recording the residual consequence they did not address: digestRows carries session_id/state/cancel/ending/ended/reasonClass while demandIdentities also carries projectId and meetingId, and voice_health_demand_sessions_update fires only on state, reason, cancel_requested_at, ending_started_at, ended_at — so an identity-only change (e.g. meeting_id backfilled) produces no event and no digest change, and the helper keeps stale identities, which record_result's session_failed path uses for identity_matches (voice-health.py:2582).

findings.title: The FLY-2693 step documents '~10 locally' but the three suites take 31-35s
findings.detail: NOT FIXED. I timed the exact step command at three heads: 31s and 35s wall (voice-health.test.py 50 tests / 15.9-18.6s, voice-health-startup-spool.test.py 4 tests, voice-health-alert-route.test.sh PASS) — about 3x the documented figure. ci-structure.test.sh passes and pins the step correctly in script-tests-6 (which .github/ci-required-jobs.json marks required), all three suite files are enumerated exactly once across the six shards, and no gate reads the comment, so this is documentation only — but the FLY-2755 six-shard rebalance uses these per-step annotations for budget planning, so an understated figure propagates into the next rebalance. Context checked this round: script-tests-6 ran 12m30s against a 20-minute budget on the current head. I also verified the adjacent concern is NOT a defect — the new step precedes 'Integration test — cmux-sync hooks' in the same job, but all three suites are fully isolated (per-invocation temp HOME, temp state roots, a private-PATH fake curl, no tmux/pkill/background processes), and the Scenario F tmux failure seen on the previous head did not recur, so the author's isolated-flake attribution is corroborated.

advisories.title: One unexpected file in the pending spool directory permanently disables the entire daemon-side health reporter across every restart
advisories.detail: NEW this round. censusSafeFiles throws on ANY directory entry not matching ^[a-f0-9]{64}\.json$ (:1092). writeAtomic creates its scratch file as `.${randomUUID()}.tmp` in that same directory (:995) and removes it only in a finally block, so a SIGKILL between open and rm leaves a permanent non-matching entry; a .DS_Store on the founder's Mac does the same. loadPendingSpools catches, calls signalUnavailable and returns false, which sets filesystemBlocked (:338-340) — and that runs exactly once per process behind the replayLoaded guard. The consequences compound: registerBoot returns false at :342-345 BEFORE startWatchdog(), so there is no 60s evaluate watchdog and no maintenance checkpoint for the process lifetime; queueAvailable() short-circuits at :776 so no observation is ever queued; and cli.ts:139 does `await health.registerBoot();` discarding the boolean. The only evidence is one console.error line (cli.ts:117-121). Net: after an ordinary crash the daemon runs for days emitting zero health data and never self-heals on restart, until an operator manually deletes the stray file. Not a false-green (the page degrades to stale/unknown), but it silently removes the daemon-side half of the feature in exactly the crash-recovery situation the feature exists for. Restrict the census to the expected filename set (ignore, or clean up, unmatched entries) instead of failing the whole load.

advisories.title: record_startup opens an episode only if demand_state is 'required' at that instant, and the duplicate short-circuit prevents re-evaluation
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. record_startup bumps phase='startup_failed', failure_count and operation='startup' even when demand is not 'required', but opens no episode and mints no intent, while still inserting the startup_events row — so every later call with the same stable startupAttemptId (= session.sessionId, voice-health-projector.ts:823) returns duplicate (:1732-1757) and re-evaluates nothing. Trigger: record-demand failing across the 60s window (execFile timeout is 500ms for a python3 cold start) leaves demand_state at 'none'. Result: no Discord alert and no incident for a session that never goes live, and since a 'desired' row is never swept by sweepVoiceSessions there is no later failed transition to re-open it. The page then shows dormant, because projectView puts demandState==='none' ahead of the phase checks, hiding phase:'startup_failed'.

advisories.title: no_action() inserts the producer_events row, so a recovery observation is consumed permanently and its incident can never be cleared
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. REPRODUCED: demand required with identity (m1,s1); session_failed(m1,s1) opens a session_unavailable episode with a pending intent; session_recovered(m1 -> successor s2) arriving while the snapshot still lists s1 returns 'no_action' and burns producerEventSeq 2; after the Bridge publishes s2, retrying the identical event returns 'duplicate' with no effect. Final state: the episode is STILL OPEN and the intent STILL 'pending' — a session that genuinely recovered leaves a permanent incident on the fixed page and an alert that can never be cleared by the legitimate recovery path. health.ts:665-688 accepts 'no_action' and splices the event out of its spool document, so the daemon never retries it either (my retry was manual). The pure race is narrow because the 3s demand tick usually publishes the successor first, but it widens to routine whenever demand_state is stale — which fail-closed-demand-never-reaches-helper makes reachable.

advisories.title: A session_ended event writes last_iteration_success_at and success_count, the poll-scope success markers
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. UPDATE health SET phase='session_ended', last_iteration_success_at = ?, last_progress_at = ?, success_count = success_count + 1 ... driven by a session-scope observation. Plan section 3 requires session recovery to write an independent sessionRecoveryProof '而不是伪造lastIterationSuccessAt', and the session_recovered branch (:2762) correctly touches only last_progress_at. Effect: the fixed page can display '最近完整成功: <now>' while the poll dependency has never succeeded and its poll_dependency episode is still open, and the heartbeat_stale anchor in evaluate_health's idle branch (:1898) is reset by an event that proves nothing about the desired poll.

advisories.title: evaluate_health has no staleness branch for starting / session_ended / session_failed / dormant / stopped
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. Only failed_retrying, idle and active are evaluated; every other phase falls to 'else: return response' (no_action) at any horizon. Combined with voice-health-projector.ts:362 mapping phase==='session_ended' unconditionally to status 'healthy', a daemon that freezes in one of those phases produces no local staleness evidence whatsoever. The only backstop is the Bridge-side 60s demand guard — which warming-lease-suppresses-startup-guard defeats for claimed/warming. Plan section 3: '首启无记录有60秒宽限，缺字段为unknown，不为健康' — there is no expiry of that grace. (The heartbeat_stale producer itself DOES work for idle and active; I verified it — see follow-ups-claims-heartbeat-stale-has-no-producer.)

advisories.title: No retention anywhere in the source store, and the 20s demand refresh appends a no-op change row plus triggers an Epic-page refresh every 60s
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED; deferred by the author at follow-ups.md:29 ('voice-health-store-has-no-retention'). The 'refreshed' branch calls _append_change unconditionally with the frozen observedAt — observed directly in my probe: four refreshes produced four byte-identical change rows. That is ~3 rows/min, ~4300/day, each a full projection snapshot of ~1-2KB; voice-health.py contains no DELETE for changes / producer_events / notification_attempts / demand_transition_events / startup_events, with wal_autocheckpoint=0 (:222) and checkpoint=False on the hot path. Measured ~1.6KB per observation => ~6MB/day steady state. Plan section 3 assumes retention exists ('retention不得删未消费事件'; test_export_rejects_deleted_change_ranges anticipates pruning). Downstream, applyVoiceHealthProjection (StateStore.ts:16589-16594) sets changed = ... || cursor.cursor !== input.cursor, true every run, so requestRefresh fires every 60s forever on a byte-identical payload — bounded by the refresher's 5s debounce and coalescing to one regeneration+publish per minute, and currently skipped for Linear-unbound projects, but an indefinite no-op publish loop once bound.

advisories.title: A curl transport failure (exit 6/7, provably nothing sent) is collapsed to delivery_unknown, which is never retried and never re-minted
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. voice_post_discord's exit status is discarded into VOICE_HTTP_CODE='000' and routed to record_voice_source_delivery delivery_unknown. delivery_unknown is absent from CLAIMABLE_STATES (voice-health.py:85 = {pending, queued_transient, config_error}) and from retryableIntentIds (voice-health-projector.ts:385-391), and _open_episode (:2098-2104) returns the existing episode's existing intent while the episode stays open, so no new intent is minted. No meta-alert fires, and 'delivery_unknown channel_id=... binding_digest=...' matches SAFE_ALERT_RECEIPT so the Bridge does not even log. Failure: the host's network drops — exactly the condition that opens the episode — curl exits 7 and the alert is lost for the whole episode. Plan section 4 draws the line at '明确未发送/429可以按既有队列重试'; curl exit 6/7 is 明确未发送 and the evidence is discarded. Fix: capture curl's exit status and route 6/7 only to queued_transient.

advisories.title: Bootstrap startup-spool events are imported only when there is exactly one demand identity
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. readStartupEvents() is invoked only under demandState==='required' && sourceStatus==='available' && identities.length === 1. With zero or two-or-more concurrent voice demands, wrapper-level startup failures (startup_config_invalid from flywheel-voice-wrapper.sh:24, etc.) are never imported, never alerted and never archived. The writer caps the spool at 128 files / 1MB (voice-health-startup-spool.py:141-145) and the overflow is swallowed by '|| true', so once saturated, later startup failures are dropped with only stderr. Plan section 4's bootstrap path expects unconditional import keyed on the Bridge's own demand association. Separately, spool/consumed/ (created at :652) has no pruning owner.

advisories.title: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is constructed with no root while every sibling in the same call gets FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR, so an isolated Bridge reads and can consume the host's production spool
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. plugin.ts:7215 computes voiceHealthStateRoot from FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR?.trim() || ~/.flywheel and passes it to readExport and the guard; three lines later readStartupEvents: createVoiceHealthStartupSpoolReader() is called with no argument and the reader resolves join(input.homeDir ?? homedir(), '.flywheel', 'voice-startup-spool') (voice-health-projector.ts:522-529), never consulting FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR. scripts/test-deploy.sh:1598 gives a 529 slot Bridge FLYWHEEL_STATE_DIR=${state} with no HOME override, so a slot Bridge reads the founder's real spool on every tick, including the blocking startup tick. If that slot's own store reports demandState 'required' / sourceStatus 'available' with exactly one identity (:751-755) it wins the .consumer.lock flock, records the production startup failure into the SLOT's health DB, and renames the production document into consumed/ (:652-660) — after which the production Bridge never mints the intent. Honest boundary: the cross-root read is unconditional and certain; the consume branch is reachable but I could not construct a slot run that reaches it, and evidence is archived rather than deleted. The homeDir parameter already exists and is used by voice-health-startup-spool-reader.test.ts:33. follow-ups.md:16 records a related deferred item warning this lock is not cross-root ownership proof.

advisories.title: validateExport's `currentProjection === undefined` guard does not catch the helper's JSON null, so a source with no health row fails every tick
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. Probed against a virgin state root: export returns "currentProjection":null (voice-health.py:3290 -> _current_projection returns None at :842 when the health row is absent). validateExport's check `(!raw.hasMore && raw.currentProjection === undefined)` uses strict equality so null passes, then record(exported.currentProjection, ...) throws in BOTH projectView (:252) and the Bridge guard (:745) — the latter BEFORE the 60s startup_not_ready waiting block. Effect on a source with no health row: the projector throws, marks the projection unavailable, logs every tick, the page shows '无法确认当前语音健康' rather than the intended '尚未采集', and the 60s guard plus the startup-spool import never run. Normally self-heals because record-demand creates the health row (confirmed by probe) and VoiceSessionRuntime.start() fires at plugin.ts:9343 before the awaited startup tick at :13414 — so the practical exposure is the startup race plus any host where record-demand can never succeed.

advisories.title: sourceStatus 'truncated' renders byte-identical to 'complete'; dropped episodes get no warning
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. projectView sets truncated when openEpisodesTruncated || notificationsTruncated || openEpisodes.length > MAX_VOICE_HEALTH_ACTIVE_INCIDENTS (:369-375) and slices to 32 at :312, but neither renderVoiceHealth reads sourceStatus except for the 'unavailable' branch. 40 open episodes render as 32 with 8 silently gone. Plan section 5 requires the 截断警示 and renderDeployment emits '状态已截断（展示 N/M）'. Aggravating: VoiceHealthView (model.ts:369-386) has no retained/total counterparts to ShuttleDeploymentView, so a warning cannot state the magnitude without a model change.

advisories.title: Every record_result branch writes source_status='available', erasing record_demand's fail-closed demand_source_unavailable marker
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. record_demand's mismatch path deliberately sets source_status='unavailable', reason_class='demand_source_unavailable', but every record_result branch (idle_success :2456, poll_failed :2477, session_failed :2517, progress :2592, session_recovered/session_ended :2773, closed_not_required :2810, daemon_stopped :2816) writes source_status='available', and idle_success additionally writes reason_class=NULL. Verified: a same-revision/different-digest snapshot gives {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: unavailable, reasonClass: demand_source_unavailable}; one ordinary idle_success later gives {demandState: unknown, sourceStatus: available, reasonClass: null}. Only demandState survives (which keeps this out of HIGH), but sourceStatus==='available' is load-bearing in the projector's startup-spool guard at :753.

advisories.title: pause() never detaches its abort listener on the timer path, and this PR newly feeds it a long-lived AbortSignal on every idle poll
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred by the author at follow-ups.md:31). pause() registers signal.addEventListener('abort', fn, {once:true}) and returns on the timer path WITHOUT removeEventListener; {once:true} only detaches after the event fires, and abort fires once at shutdown. This PR introduced the exposure: pre-PR daemon.ts called options.sleep(idlePollMs) with NO signal (verified against e82193650:daemon.ts:244,309), whereas the new run() passes this.sleepController.signal — one AbortController per daemon (daemon.ts:302) — at daemon.ts:326 (idle poll) and :348 (failure backoff), and cli.ts:357 wires sleep: pause. One listener is permanently retained per idle poll: 12/min at the FLYWHEEL_VOICE_IDLE_POLL_MS default of 5000, ~17k/day, each closing over a distinct timer handle and resolve. I checked: Node emits NO MaxListenersExceededWarning for AbortSignal at 40 listeners, so the growth is silent; on shutdown all accumulated listeners fire at once. One removeEventListener in the timer path closes it.

advisories.title: claim/renew install the lease from an unvalidated body.leaseTtlMs, so a malformed 2xx produces a NaN deadline that never fences plus a 1ms timer spin
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. This PR rewrote the request layer specifically so a 2xx is not assumed successful and added strict decoding for /desired (decodeDesired at :153), but claim (:306), renew (:332) and renewRecovered (:352) still pass body.leaseTtlMs straight into VoiceLease.install, whose only typing is a compile-time generic on a network response. With leaseTtlMs absent or non-numeric, deadlineMs = sentAt + NaN - timeout = NaN (:105); VoiceLease.assert() then evaluates `!active || monoNow() >= NaN` = false and never throws, so the fence — the mechanism stopping two daemons from both believing they hold authority — is silently disabled for the session. SessionLifetime.armDeadline (daemon.ts:214-228) re-arms with lease.remainingMs = NaN, which Node coerces to a 1ms delay, producing a ~1000/s re-arm spin. A Number.isSafeInteger guard in install() closes both.

advisories.title: record_delivery has no post-timeout idempotency key, so a worker cannot confirm its own committed write
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. The authorization side is sound — 'sent' requires a matching claim_token, matching binding_digest, intent['channel_id'] == channel_id and snowflake-validated ids, so no fabricated success — but the UPDATE clears claim_token, claimed_at and claim_expires_at. A retry after a 500ms execFile timeout that actually committed returns notification_claim_mismatch, indistinguishable from a genuinely wrong claim. Plan section 3 requires '超时后不能假设未提交：用 ... 重试查询去重记录'. Every other mutating command has such a key (generation+producerEventSeq, startupAttemptId, revision/cursor, claim token).

advisories.title: voice_health_demand_events is retention-protected forever while the consuming cursor is in-memory, so Bridge restarts replay the whole history
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/teamlead/voice_health_demand_events.json classifies the table protectedCurrentOrReference, which fly-2006-retention-loader.mjs treats as a non-delete category — so the append-only trigger log in the shared production teamlead DB grows one row per voice_sessions insert/delete/state/reason/cancel/ending/ended change, forever. VoiceSessionRuntime.demandCursor is a plain in-memory field reset to 0 on every Bridge restart, and projectVoiceDemand drains one 200-event page per 3s tick, so catch-up after restart costs N/200 x 3s for N lifetime events. During catch-up refreshObservedAt is false (events non-empty) so demand_observed_at is not refreshed — which, given the 90s gate in stale-gate-uses-frozen-data-clock, means the page shows '读数过期' for the entire catch-up window. Plan section 3 anticipated retention that deletes consumed events only.

advisories.title: demandEvent() drops cancelRequested / endingStarted / previousState, so the helper cannot tell a cancelled demand from a dependency failure
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. The trigger records cancel_requested, ending_started, ended and old_state (StateStore.ts:2810-2859) precisely so the helper can distinguish 'user cancelled' from 'system failed it', but the recorder forwards only eventSeq/eventKind/demandId/attemptId/observedAt (+reasonClass for 'failed'). Failure: a founder cancels a meeting, the session goes ending then times out, and voiceHealthReasonClass maps ending_timeout to session_runtime_failed — the helper opens a session_unavailable incident and pages the engineering channel for a user-initiated cancel. Plan section 3 (防止失败后自动消警) requires the cancel fact to be carried into the record.

advisories.title: claim/setState/outbound/receipt failures propagate to the poll path and are recorded as poll_dependency, which a later idle_success closes
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. runOnce() lets bridge.claim() and the lifetime bridge calls throw out to run()'s catch, where pollFailure() records kind:'poll_failed' carrying the diagnostic's operation (claim/state/outbound/receipt). voice-health.py:2498 opens a poll_dependency episode for those, and _close_poll_episode closes it on the next idle_success — so a failure to join the room is cleared by an unrelated idle poll, the scope-isolation outcome plan section 3 forbids. Partially mitigated because the demand path independently opens session_unavailable on required->failed and the 60s waiting guard covers 'desired' sessions, so this is noise plus premature recovery rather than total blindness.

advisories.title: A failure to report the terminal session state to the Bridge is swallowed with no health observation
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. Both terminal paths wrap bridge.setState in try/catch, set terminalConfirmed=false and only console.error('[voice] session terminal receipt unavailable; recovery state retained'). Before this change the error propagated out of runOnce and was counted by run()'s catch. Now the Bridge round-trip failure produces no poll_failed and no session_failed observation, no episode and no alert — a whole class of bridge_* failures on the terminal path is invisible to the ledger this change exists to build. recover() (daemon.ts:365-413) likewise emits no health observation on the equivalent path.

advisories.title: A 135s real-wall-clock test whose iteration-count assertion tolerates only one lost iteration
advisories.detail: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. Commit 868800fff (the only code change since my last review) replaced the per-entry host-clock comparison with a set-membership check on submitted observedAt values — I verified that fix is correct and effective: required-wall-clock-thresholds.test.ts passes 1/1 locally at this head, the new assertion is sound (lastIterationSuccessAt always originates from a submitted observation via both the direct branch in observeNormal and the flushAggregate branch), and it does not weaken the heartbeat coverage. But the flakiness substance is untouched: RUN_FOR_MS is still 135_000 (:20) with await sleep(5000) per iteration, and the assertions are still successes >= 26 (:70) and lastHeartbeat.successCount >= 24 (:95). At zero overhead the loop yields exactly 27 iterations, so the margin is ONE lost iteration; ~185ms average per-iteration drift drops it to 26 and ~400ms drops it to 25 and fails — while each iteration drives an fsync'd atomic spool write and a python3 spawn on the drain path. Honest counter-evidence: it has now been green on CI twice (Unit (light) 7m9s of a 25-minute budget) and three times locally at 135.2-135.5s. Deriving the expected count from measured elapsed time would remove the risk entirely.

advisories.title: config_error and invalid receipts retry every 30s forever with no cap, no backoff and no dead-letter transition
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred at follow-ups.md:32). VoiceHealthAlertDispatcher.drain treats config_error and any unparsable receipt as a retry and calls scheduleRetry with a fixed 30s delay, unbounded. lead-alert.sh returns config_error for permanent conditions (missing helper, failed route preflight, invalid frozen payload), so a misconfigured route spawns /bin/bash lead-alert.sh every 30s for the daemon's lifetime; the Bridge does the same every 60s (voice-health-projector.ts:385-392). claim_notification increments attempt_count but nothing enforces a limit or a dead_lettered transition. meta-alert.sh's 10-minute per-reason debounce bounds the alert noise, but not the process churn or the growing attempt_count.

advisories.title: The voice-health tick is the only projector awaited ahead of gatePoller.start(); bounded, but an unnecessary boot dependency
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. Bounded and not a real availability risk, per measurement. Ceiling is ~265 sequential helper calls (two drains of <=32 pages, 1 evaluate, <=128 spool record-startup, <=8 waiting record-startup), each capped by execFile timeout: 500 (:413, :708) plus <=128 lock acquisitions at readyTimeoutMs: 500 (:626) — ~196s absolute worst case, but that requires all 265 calls to SUCCEED just under 500ms, since any rejection short-circuits run() into markVoiceHealthProjectionUnavailable. No hang risk: scripts/lib/voice-health.py has zero hits for subprocess|Popen|os.system|os.fork. Measured ~45ms/call, so a typical boot is ~0.15s and a full 128-event spool ~6-12s. Flagged only because the two sibling projectors constructed just above (:12199-12201) live solely in the async 3s poller, whose rejections GatePoller already catches and logs (gate-poller.ts:640-647); dropping the pre-start await costs at most one poll cycle of freshness.

advisories.title: The new TypeScript route/bindingDigest module has zero production importers
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED (deferred at follow-ups.md:30). A repo-wide grep for 'voice-health-alert-route' outside dist finds exactly one importer: packages/teamlead/src/__tests__/voice-health-alert-delivery.test.ts. Production route resolution happens entirely in scripts/lead-alert.sh via node scripts/shuttle-route-bindings.mjs, and the bindingDigest persisted and revalidated by the helper comes from that shell path — not from resolveVoiceHealthAlertRoute, which computes a different digest (sha256 over {schemaVersion, originProject, route}). The repo now carries two independent definitions of the same contract, only one of which ships. Coverage of the shipped path is not missing (scripts/__tests__/voice-health-alert-route.test.sh exercises the real shell sender and passes), so the cost is drift risk plus a TS test that looks like production routing coverage but is not. Wire it up or delete it.

advisories.title: main() reads stdin unconditionally for every subcommand, so any caller that does not close stdin hangs forever with no deadline
advisories.detail: NEW this round. `payload = _read_payload()` runs before the command dispatch, so even `init` — which then requires the payload to be None or {} — blocks on an open stdin. PROVEN: `timeout 4 python3 scripts/lib/voice-health.py --state-root $TMP init < <(sleep 30)` exits 124 (hung), while the same command with `</dev/null` exits 0. The helper has no internal deadline. Production callers are safe (the TS clients call child.stdin.end() and additionally bound with timeout: 500; lead-alert.sh pipes via printf which closes stdin), but the author documented in engineering/doc/milestones/FLY-2693.md that this already cost them debugging time on macOS, and any future runbook, cron or QA script that invokes the helper without redirecting stdin will hang indefinitely. Read stdin only for the commands that take a payload, or only when it is not a TTY.

advisories.title: A shipped follow-ups entry asserts heartbeat_stale has no producer; it does
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. follow-ups.md:28 states '保留 follow-up MEDIUM heartbeat-stale-never-produced：heartbeat_stale reason 已声明但尚无 producer'. I disproved this against the real helper: register-boot, record-demand(required), one idle_success at 10:00:10, then evaluate at 10:00:50 -> no_action (correct, <60s); evaluate at 10:01:30 -> status=recorded, episode.reasonClass=heartbeat_stale, with a notification intent minted; evaluate at 10:05:00 -> no_action (correct, episode already open). evaluate_health's idle and active branches (voice-health.py:1898, :1903) are the producers, and both the Bridge guard (voice-health-projector.ts:739) and the daemon watchdog (health.ts:425) call evaluate. The real gap is narrower and already covered by evaluate-missing-stale-branch-for-terminal-phases. This matters because the document ships with the change and a Lead prioritising follow-ups would schedule work to build a producer that already exists.

advisories.title: reportFatalStartupFailure discards the error entirely, leaving zero diagnostic for a daemon that will not start
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. The parameter is named _error and the log line is the constant '[voice] fatal reasonClass=startup_not_ready operation=startup'; the spool record carries only the reasonClass. This follows plan section 3's rule that raw Error.message must not reach stderr, and package-onboard-smoke.test.sh:232 asserts the exact string. The cost is that 'voice will not start' — the originating FLY-2693 symptom — produces no locally recoverable detail anywhere. A bounded closed-vocabulary classifier (e.g. mapping the known config errors to startup_config_invalid) would keep the sanitization and restore triage.

advisories.title: validateVoiceBridgeUrl hard-fails any non-loopback BRIDGE_URL with no allowlist
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. loadVoiceDaemonConfig throws voice_bridge_url_invalid for any host that is not localhost, [::1] or 127.x.x.x, which the wrapper turns into voice_config_invalid and exit 0. Plan section 2 said '生产默认loopback' and '跨主机部署如存在，按现有可信配置明确allowlist'; no allowlist was implemented, so this is an unannounced hard break for any host configuring a non-loopback Bridge. ::ffff:127.0.0.1 is also unmatched.

advisories.title: The voice alert lane silently inherits SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE as a permission-preflight override
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. VOICE_HEALTH_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-${SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE:-} means a stale or leaked SHUTTLE_ROUTE_PERMISSION_FIXTURE in the environment also replaces the real Discord VIEW_CHANNEL/SEND_MESSAGES preflight for voice alerts (shuttle-route-bindings.mjs:301-309). A QA harness that exports it and forgets to unset it downgrades a second production lane's sender check with no signal.

advisories.title: The frozen-payload openedAt gate is prefix-only while every sibling field is fully anchored
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T") has no end anchor, and the value is interpolated into the Discord BODY at :778. Not exploitable today — the writer validates via _parse_timestamp (voice-health.py:714), jq -n --arg prevents payload injection, and allowed_mentions:{parse:[]} blocks pings — but it is the one unanchored field in an otherwise closed-vocabulary gate. Related latent fragility: jq errors with exit 5 on `null | test(...)`, so any _open_episode call site leaving health.operation NULL would make its alert permanently undeliverable as 'frozen notification payload is invalid'; I re-checked all five call sites and each sets operation first, so this is latent only.

advisories.title: The demand digest omits project_name and meeting_id, and neither column is in the trigger's UPDATE OF list
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED, and deliberate: follow-ups.md:14 dispositions this as '已处理 demand-digest-field-scope-undefined ... 无关字段更新不改变 revision/digest'. Recording the residual consequence they did not address: digestRows carries session_id/state/cancel/ending/ended/reasonClass while demandIdentities also carries projectId and meetingId, and voice_health_demand_sessions_update fires only on state, reason, cancel_requested_at, ending_started_at, ended_at — so an identity-only change (e.g. meeting_id backfilled) produces no event and no digest change, and the helper keeps stale identities, which record_result's session_failed path uses for identity_matches (voice-health.py:2582).

advisories.title: The FLY-2693 step documents '~10 locally' but the three suites take 31-35s
advisories.detail: NOT FIXED. I timed the exact step command at three heads: 31s and 35s wall (voice-health.test.py 50 tests / 15.9-18.6s, voice-health-startup-spool.test.py 4 tests, voice-health-alert-route.test.sh PASS) — about 3x the documented figure. ci-structure.test.sh passes and pins the step correctly in script-tests-6 (which .github/ci-required-jobs.json marks required), all three suite files are enumerated exactly once across the six shards, and no gate reads the comment, so this is documentation only — but the FLY-2755 six-shard rebalance uses these per-step annotations for budget planning, so an understated figure propagates into the next rebalance. Context checked this round: script-tests-6 ran 12m30s against a 20-minute budget on the current head. I also verified the adjacent concern is NOT a defect — the new step precedes 'Integration test — cmux-sync hooks' in the same job, but all three suites are fully isolated (per-invocation temp HOME, temp state roots, a private-PATH fake curl, no tmux/pkill/background processes), and the Scenario F tmux failure seen on the previous head did not recur, so the author's isolated-flake attribution is corroborated.
